senses.definition: (countable and uncountable) A colour like that of chocolate or coffee.
examples: The browns and greens in this painting give it a nice woodsy feel.
He wore brown jeans for his birthday.

senses.definition: (snooker, countable) One of the colour balls used in snooker, with a value of 4 points.
(uncountable) Black tar heroin.
(slang, archaic, countable) A copper coin.

quotes.text: “To save a journey up the town, / A razor lent here for a brown: / But if you think the price too high, / I beg you won’t the razor try.”
quotes.reference: 1851, Henry Mayhew, London Labour and the London Poor, published 1861:

quotes.text: I know there are many persons — some who are themselves poor — who 'never turn a beggar from their door,' but always give them a few browns (halfpence) or some scran (broken victuals).
quotes.reference: 1853, Charles John Chetwynd Talbot, Meliora, Or, Better Times to Come, page 247:

quotes.text:
"We've not had any breakfast,—won't you toss us down a brown?"—
That's what they call a penny in the streets of London Town.

senses.definition: A brown horse or other animal.

quotes.text: […] browns are the soberest, bays are the worst tempered, and chestnuts are the most foolish.
quotes.reference: 1877, George Nevile, Horses and Riding, page 105:

senses.definition: (sometimes capitalised, countable, informal, ethnic slur) A person of mostly Latin American (or Latino), Middle Eastern/North African, South Asian, and sometimes Southeast Asian, Pacific Islander, or rarely Native American descent; a brown-skinned person; someone of mulatto, or biracial appearance.

quotes.text: Many browns and blacks are immigrants — some of whom have not yet become naturalized citizens of the United States.
quotes.reference: 2005, Kristen A. Myers, Racetalk: Racism Hiding in Plain Sight:

quotes.text: For example, a Brown Asian Caucus emerged at the inaugural National Conference on Asian American Mental Health in 1972 – where Filipinos were joined by Pacific Islanders who also felt marginalized as part of the Asian American/ Pacific Islander (AAPI) umbrella group.
quotes.reference: 2020, Kevin L. Nadal, The Brown Asian American Movement: Advocating for South Asian, Southeast Asian, and Filipino American Communities:

senses.definition: (entomology) Any of various nymphalid butterflies of subfamily Satyrinae (formerly the family Satyridae), such as those of the genera Heteronympha and Melanitis.
(informal) A brown trout (Salmo trutta).
(hunting, as "the brown") A mass of birds or animals that may be indiscriminately fired at.

quotes.text: The temptation to have a shot into the brown was great. There was not a head there which was not a big one and the one by himself was not too easy a shot since it is always difficult to shoot when lying in soft snow.
quotes.reference: 1928, R. Pigot, Twenty-five Years Big Game Hunting, page 166:

quotes.text: My anger mounted at this, I opened the courtyard door and raised my musket to fire into the brown; I had loaded it with small shot, and if it had gone off that would have been the death of us and the ruin of all of us in the house.

senses.definition: Having a brown colour.

quotes.text: But none of those brown dwarfs were speeding along on a trajectory that would carry them out of the galaxy like “runaway” hypervelocity stars observed by astronomers in the last two decades.

senses.definition: (obsolete) Gloomy.
(sometimes capitalized) Of or relating to any of various ethnic groups having dark pigmentation of the skin.

quotes.text:

The saddest part is that I don’t think they understand why it’s insulting to ask a brown person for a passport.

quotes.text:

I think there is in the sort of South Asian, you know, psyche, a kind of adoration of Western ideals and culture that was sort of implanted into us by the British, you know, and this idea that everything that is Western is superior and better than what we have and what India--you know, what is true to our own culture.

examples: Fry the onions until they brown.

quotes.text: The chicken was browning nicely, the skin beginning to crisp and take on the toasty tones of oiled wood.
quotes.reference: 2006, Michael Pollan, The Omnivore's Dilemma, The Penguin Press, →ISBN, page 269:

quotes.text:
Don't microwave your milk too long
It browns and bubbles over

senses.definition: (intransitive, transitive) To tan.
examples: Light-skinned people tend to brown when exposed to the sun.

senses.definition: (transitive) To make brown or dusky.

quotes.text: A trembling twilight o'er the welkin moves, / Browns the dim void and darkens deep the groves.

senses.definition: (transitive) To give a bright brown colour to, as to gun barrels, by forming a thin coating of oxide on their surface.

quotes.text: It is mixed uniformly with olive oil, and rubbed upon the iron slightly heated, which is afterwards exposed to the air, till the wished-for degree of browning is produced.
